packet.headline_seed: Ex-cricket captains urge 'proper medical care' for Imran Khan
packet.description_seed: The former skippers say it is "basic decency" for Pakistan to comply with a court-ordered medical assessment.

what: Ex-cricket captains urge 'proper medical care' for Imran Khan

clean_source_blocks.text: The former skippers say it is "basic decency" for Pakistan to comply with a court-ordered medical assessment.

Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and 19 former captains urged Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to ensure independent medical assessment, treatment and court-ordered family visits for Imran Khan. Former India captains Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are among 21 former international captains who have appealed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for proper medical treatment and welfare of jailed former Prime Minister and World Cup winning captain Imran Khan. The move has been initiated by former Australia captain Greg Chappell and marks the second letter by former international ca...

The former cricket captains laid out three demands in their letter, the first of which is that Khan be assessed by a medical board directed by Pakistan's Supreme Court – which would include his personal physicians – particularly on the reported loss of vision in his right eye. They also urged authorities to allow weekly visits by Khan's family, as ordered by the court, "without interruptions or administrative delays". Finally, they asked that any treatment recommended by the medical board be "provided without delay". "Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody," read the letter initiated by former Australian captain Greg Chappell. "Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request."

A group of 21 former international cricket captains, including India's Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, signed a letter to Pakistan's government yesterday (23 August) regarding the health care of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan. Khan has been in jail since 2023 and was sentenced late last year along with his wife to 17 years on corruption charges they both deny. The 73-year-old, who was also a former Pakistan cricket captain, was transferred back to jail on Friday hours after he was taken to hospital for court-ordered medical checks. The Supreme Court had ordered earlier in the week that Khan be taken to the private Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad for treatment after his lawyers filed a petition over health concerns.

Imran Khan, shown here in 2022, has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges which he denies

A group of former cricket captains, including Indian batting legend Sunil Gavaskar and one of England's longest-serving skippers Sir Alastair Cook, have called on Pakistan to ensure its ex-PM Imran Khan be given proper care while in custody.

The cricketer-turned-politician has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges which he denies.

In a letter to Pakistan's current leader Shehbaz Sharif, the 21 former skippers aired concern that Khan, 73, was allowed "only a few hours" at a hospital last week where he was examined by a state-appointed team.

Khan's party has also filed a contempt petition against the government for not giving him access to his own doctors, as ordered by the top court.

The former cricket captains laid out three demands in their letter, the first of which is that Khan be assessed by a medical board directed by Pakistan's Supreme Court – which would include his personal physicians – particularly on the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

They also urged authorities to allow weekly visits by Khan's family, as ordered by the court, "without interruptions or administrative delays".

Finally, they asked that any treatment recommended by the medical board be "provided without delay".

"Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody," read the letter initiated by former Australian captain Greg Chappell.

"Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request."

Among the other signatories were England's Michael Atherton, Michael Brearley, Nasser Hussain, Andrew Strauss and David Gower, India's Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, and Australia's Belinda Clark, Adam Gilchrist, Steve Waugh and Kim Hughes.

Fourteen of the former skippers had also supported an earlier appeal for "humane treatment and proper medical care" for Khan which was submitted in February.

Khan's lawyer claimed at the time that his client had 15% vision left in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

The signatories of both letters had described themselves as "former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field", adding that the bond "transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries".

[Lähde: The Business Standard | URL: https://www.tbsnews.net/world/former-cricket-captains-appeal-pakistan-over-khan-health-care-1523086]
A group of 21 former international cricket captains, including India's Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, signed a letter to Pakistan's government yesterday (23 August) regarding the health care of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.

Khan has been in jail since 2023 and was sentenced late last year along with his wife to 17 years on corruption charges they both deny.

The 73-year-old, who was also a former Pakistan cricket captain, was transferred back to jail on Friday hours after he was taken to hospital for court-ordered medical checks.

The Supreme Court had ordered earlier in the week that Khan be taken to the private Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad for treatment after his lawyers filed a petition over health concerns.

The cricket captains' statement, which followed an earlier letter in February about Khan's medical treatment, laid out three requests.

Firstly, they asked that the medical board directed by the Supreme Court "be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment" of Khan's health, "particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye".

Secondly, they requested that the weekly visits by Khan's family reinstated by the court "be honoured without interruption or administrative delay".

Their final request was that the treatment mandated after the medical assessment "be provided without delay".

Signatories also included Dilip Vengsarkar (India), Michael Atherton, Michael Brearley, Nasser Hussain, Andrew Strauss and David Gower (England), Allan Border, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Adam Gilchrist, Steve Waugh and Kim Hughes (Australia), Clive Lloyd (West Indies) and John Wright (New Zealand).

Khan was prime minister from 2018 to 2022 before being removed in a no-confidence vote during a political crisis over tensions between his government and Pakistan's powerful military establishment.

He has since faced multiple legal cases on corruption and other charges.

Khan and his party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, maintain that the cases against him are politically motivated.

His arrest triggered nationwide protests in May 2023, some of which turned violent and led to hundreds of arrests.

payload.title: Entiset krikettikapteenit vaativat Imran Khanille asianmukaista hoitoa
payload.summary: Kaksikymmentäyksi entistä kansainvälistä krikettikapteenia vaatii Pakistanin hallitusta toteuttamaan Imran Khanin lääkärintarkastukset, hoidon ja perhetapaamiset oikeuden määräysten mukaisesti.
payload.content:
Joukko 21 entistä kansainvälistä krikettikapteenia on vedonnut Pakistanin pääministeriin Shehbaz Sharifiin, jotta vangitun entisen pääministerin Imran Khanin terveydentila arvioitaisiin riippumattomasti ja hänen tarvitsemansa hoito järjestettäisiin. Allekirjoittajat vaativat myös oikeuden määräämien perhetapaamisten toteuttamista ja katsovat, ettei 73-vuotiaan Khanin lääketieteellinen kohtelu saa jäädä hänen tapaukseensa liittyvien oikeudellisten tai poliittisten kiistojen varjoon.

## Vetoomuksessa esitetään kolme vaatimusta

Australian entisen kapteenin Greg Chappellin aloitteesta laaditun kirjeen allekirjoittajiin kuuluvat muun muassa Intian entiset kapteenit Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev ja Dilip Vengsarkar. Pakistanin hallitukselle 23. elokuuta osoitettu vetoomus sisältää kolme konkreettista vaatimusta, jotka koskevat lääkärinarviota, yhteydenpitoa perheeseen ja arvioinnin perusteella suositeltua hoitoa. Vetoomuksen taustalla on huoli tuomioistuimen määräysten toteutumisesta käytännössä.

Ensimmäiseksi ryhmä pyytää, että Khanin tutkisi Pakistanin korkeimman oikeuden määräämä lääkärilautakunta, johon kuuluisi myös hänen omia lääkäreitään. Lautakunnan pitäisi tehdä riippumaton arvio Khanin terveydestä ja mahdollisesta hoidon tarpeesta. Arviossa olisi kirjeen mukaan kiinnitettävä erityistä huomiota tietoihin Khanin oikean silmän näön heikkenemisestä. Kyse on raportoidusta terveyshuolesta, ei lähteissä vahvistetusta diagnoosista.

Toiseksi allekirjoittajat vaativat Khanin perheelle viikoittaisia tapaamisia, jotka oikeus on jo määrännyt. Tapaamisten pitäisi toteutua ilman keskeytyksiä tai hallinnollisia viivytyksiä. Kolmanneksi lääkärilautakunnan mahdollisesti suosittelemat hoidot olisi järjestettävä viipymättä. Kirjeessä korostetaan, että oikeuden määräämän lääketieteellisen prosessin loppuun saattaminen on perusinhimillistä asianmukaisuutta eikä tapauksen muista kiistoista riippuva vaatimus.

## Khan palautettiin sairaalasta vankilaan

Khan on ollut vankilassa vuodesta 2023, ja kapteenien kirjeen mukaan hän on viettänyt säilössä yli kolme vuotta. Hänet ja hänen vaimonsa tuomittiin loppuvuodesta 2025 korruptiosyytteiden perusteella 17 vuoden vankeuteen, mutta kumpikin kiistää syytteet. Pakistanin entisenä pääministerinä tunnettu Khan on myös maan entinen krikettikapteeni ja maailmanmestaruuden voittanut kapteeni.

Pakistanin korkein oikeus määräsi aiemmin viikolla, että Khan on vietävä Islamabadissa sijaitsevaan yksityiseen Shifa International Hospital -sairaalaan hoitoa varten. Määräys annettiin sen jälkeen, kun hänen asianajajansa olivat jättäneet terveydentilaa koskevan vetoomuksen. Khan vietiin perjantaina sairaalaan oikeuden määräämiin lääketieteellisiin tutkimuksiin, mutta hänet siirrettiin takaisin vankilaan jo muutaman tunnin kuluttua.

article.description: Kaksikymmentäyksi entistä kansainvälistä krikettikapteenia vaatii Pakistanin hallitusta toteuttamaan Imran Khanin lääkärintarkastukset, hoidon ja perhetapaamiset oikeuden määräysten mukaisesti.

Imran Khan, shown here in 2022, has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges which he denies

A group of former cricket captains, including Indian batting legend Sunil Gavaskar and one of England's longest-serving skippers Sir Alastair Cook, have called on Pakistan to ensure its ex-PM Imran Khan be given proper care while in custody.

The cricketer-turned-politician has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges which he denies.

In a letter to Pakistan's current leader Shehbaz Sharif, the 21 former skippers aired concern that Khan, 73, was allowed "only a few hours" at a hospital last week where he was examined by a state-appointed team.

Khan's party has also filed a contempt petition against the government for not giving him access to his own doctors, as ordered by the top court.

The former cricket captains laid out three demands in their letter, the first of which is that Khan be assessed by a medical board directed by Pakistan's Supreme Court – which would include his personal physicians – particularly on the reported loss of vision in his right eye.

They also urged authorities to allow weekly visits by Khan's family, as ordered by the court, "without interruptions or administrative delays".

Finally, they asked that any treatment recommended by the medical board be "provided without delay".

"Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody," read the letter initiated by former Australian captain Greg Chappell.

"Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request."

Among the other signatories were England's Michael Atherton, Michael Brearley, Nasser Hussain, Andrew Strauss and David Gower, India's Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, and Australia's Belinda Clark, Adam Gilchrist, Steve Waugh and Kim Hughes.

Fourteen of the former skippers had also supported an earlier appeal for "humane treatment and proper medical care" for Khan which was submitted in February.

Khan's lawyer claimed at the time that his client had 15% vision left in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action.

The signatories of both letters had described themselves as "former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field", adding that the bond "transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries".

[Lähde: The Business Standard | URL: https://www.tbsnews.net/world/former-cricket-captains-appeal-pakistan-over-khan-health-care-1523086]
A group of 21 former international cricket captains, including India's Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, signed a letter to Pakistan's government yesterday (23 August) regarding the health care of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan.

Khan has been in jail since 2023 and was sentenced late last year along with his wife to 17 years on corruption charges they both deny.

The 73-year-old, who was also a former Pakistan cricket captain, was transferred back to jail on Friday hours after he was taken to hospital for court-ordered medical checks.

The Supreme Court had ordered earlier in the week that Khan be taken to the private Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad for treatment after his lawyers filed a petition over health concerns.

The cricket captains' statement, which followed an earlier letter in February about Khan's medical treatment, laid out three requests.

Firstly, they asked that the medical board directed by the Supreme Court "be permitted to complete a full and independent assessment" of Khan's health, "particularly the reported loss of vision in his right eye".

Secondly, they requested that the weekly visits by Khan's family reinstated by the court "be honoured without interruption or administrative delay".

Their final request was that the treatment mandated after the medical assessment "be provided without delay".

Signatories also included Dilip Vengsarkar (India), Michael Atherton, Michael Brearley, Nasser Hussain, Andrew Strauss and David Gower (England), Allan Border, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Adam Gilchrist, Steve Waugh and Kim Hughes (Australia), Clive Lloyd (West Indies) and John Wright (New Zealand).

Khan was prime minister from 2018 to 2022 before being removed in a no-confidence vote during a political crisis over tensions between his government and Pakistan's powerful military establishment.

He has since faced multiple legal cases on corruption and other charges.

Khan and his party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, maintain that the cases against him are politically motivated.

His arrest triggered nationwide protests in May 2023, some of which turned violent and led to hundreds of arrests.

article.content:
Joukko 21 entistä kansainvälistä krikettikapteenia on vedonnut Pakistanin pääministeriin Shehbaz Sharifiin, jotta vangitun entisen pääministerin Imran Khanin terveydentila arvioitaisiin riippumattomasti ja hänen tarvitsemansa hoito järjestettäisiin. Allekirjoittajat vaativat myös oikeuden määräämien perhetapaamisten toteuttamista ja katsovat, ettei 73-vuotiaan Khanin lääketieteellinen kohtelu saa jäädä hänen tapaukseensa liittyvien oikeudellisten tai poliittisten kiistojen varjoon.

## Vetoomuksessa esitetään kolme vaatimusta

Australian entisen kapteenin Greg Chappellin aloitteesta laaditun kirjeen allekirjoittajiin kuuluvat muun muassa Intian entiset kapteenit Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev ja Dilip Vengsarkar. Pakistanin hallitukselle 23. elokuuta osoitettu vetoomus sisältää kolme konkreettista vaatimusta, jotka koskevat lääkärinarviota, yhteydenpitoa perheeseen ja arvioinnin perusteella suositeltua hoitoa. Vetoomuksen taustalla on huoli tuomioistuimen määräysten toteutumisesta käytännössä.

Ensimmäiseksi ryhmä pyytää, että Khanin tutkisi Pakistanin korkeimman oikeuden määräämä lääkärilautakunta, johon kuuluisi myös hänen omia lääkäreitään. Lautakunnan pitäisi tehdä riippumaton arvio Khanin terveydestä ja mahdollisesta hoidon tarpeesta. Arviossa olisi kirjeen mukaan kiinnitettävä erityistä huomiota tietoihin Khanin oikean silmän näön heikkenemisestä. Kyse on raportoidusta terveyshuolesta, ei lähteissä vahvistetusta diagnoosista.

Toiseksi allekirjoittajat vaativat Khanin perheelle viikoittaisia tapaamisia, jotka oikeus on jo määrännyt. Tapaamisten pitäisi toteutua ilman keskeytyksiä tai hallinnollisia viivytyksiä. Kolmanneksi lääkärilautakunnan mahdollisesti suosittelemat hoidot olisi järjestettävä viipymättä. Kirjeessä korostetaan, että oikeuden määräämän lääketieteellisen prosessin loppuun saattaminen on perusinhimillistä asianmukaisuutta eikä tapauksen muista kiistoista riippuva vaatimus.

## Khan palautettiin sairaalasta vankilaan

Khan on ollut vankilassa vuodesta 2023, ja kapteenien kirjeen mukaan hän on viettänyt säilössä yli kolme vuotta. Hänet ja hänen vaimonsa tuomittiin loppuvuodesta 2025 korruptiosyytteiden perusteella 17 vuoden vankeuteen, mutta kumpikin kiistää syytteet. Pakistanin entisenä pääministerinä tunnettu Khan on myös maan entinen krikettikapteeni ja maailmanmestaruuden voittanut kapteeni.

Pakistanin korkein oikeus määräsi aiemmin viikolla, että Khan on vietävä Islamabadissa sijaitsevaan yksityiseen Shifa International Hospital -sairaalaan hoitoa varten. Määräys annettiin sen jälkeen, kun hänen asianajajansa olivat jättäneet terveydentilaa koskevan vetoomuksen. Khan vietiin perjantaina sairaalaan oikeuden määräämiin lääketieteellisiin tutkimuksiin, mutta hänet siirrettiin takaisin vankilaan jo muutaman tunnin kuluttua.
